_doc: Per-tool annotation-CLASSIFICATION ratchet for story-mcp (rf2-yi451; closed-world list corrected rf2-voux7 finding 4). See the sibling re-frame2-pair-classifications.json _doc for the full rationale. POSTURES: `read-only` = readOnlyHint:true MUST be set + destructiveHint MUST NOT be true; `destructive` = destructiveHint:true MUST be set + readOnlyHint MUST NOT be true (the safety-load-bearing write surface — register-variant / unregister-variant / record-as-variant are the gated `--allow-writes` writers; preview-variant / run-variant execute a variant lifecycle so they carry destructiveHint). story-mcp is CLOSED-WORLD: EVERY tool reaches only JVM-side / on-box story-registry state, never an external system — its three annotation defs (read-only-annotations, destructive-write-annotations, run-variant-annotations in tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/schemas.cljc) ALL set `:openWorldHint false`, and that false value rides verbatim onto the live tools/list descriptor. (rf2-voux7 finding 4: the pre-fix _doc wrongly claimed descriptors carry openWorldHint:true — confusing the generated manifest's `:annotations` KEY-presence vector, which lists `openWorldHint` because the key EXISTS, with its VALUE, which is false. The empty `closed-world: []` therefore pinned NOTHING, blessing a silent flip of any tool to openWorldHint:true.) Because story-mcp is wholly closed-world, the `closed-world` list below pins EVERY tool to openWorldHint:false — a flip on any tool turns the ratchet RED. Sourced from tools/story-mcp/tool-descriptors.edn — keep in lockstep; one row per tool.
